saved_note.visit_summary: Right lower lobe pneumonia in a patient with heart failure: outpatient amoxicillin-clavulanate plus clarithromycin, heart medicines continued; chest x-ray and labs today, recheck in 2 days.

items.text: Cough for 5 days with fevers and chills for 2 days.
Cough for 5 days productive of thick yellow-green sputum, with fevers and chills for the past 2 days.
Right-sided chest pain with deep breaths.
More short of breath than usual; winded walking to the mailbox.
Weight steady at 204 pounds; ankle swelling unchanged; sleeps on 2 pillows as usual.
Grandson had a bad cold last week.
Former smoker; quit 11 years ago.
No new orthopnea or change in leg swelling.
Temperature 100.9, heart rate 92, respiratory rate 20, BP 128/78, oxygen saturation 94%.
Crackles at the right lung base; regular heart sounds without a new murmur; trace ankle edema, unchanged.
Not discussed
Community-acquired pneumonia of the right lower lung, suitable for outpatient treatment with close follow-up.
Heart failure: weight stable, no new orthopnea, trace ankle edema unchanged.
Chest x-ray today; complete blood count and basic metabolic panel.
Start amoxicillin-clavulanate 875 mg twice daily and clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily, both for 7 days.
Continue carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, furosemide 40 mg in the morning, lisinopril 20 mg, spironolactone 25 mg, potassium chloride 20 mEq daily and simvastatin 40 mg at night.
Fluids within the usual limit of about 2 liters a day; acetaminophen up to 1,000 mg every 8 hours for fever.
Check home pulse oximetry twice daily; go to the ER for worse breathing, oxygen below 92, confusion or inability to keep fluids down.
Office to call with the x-ray result this afternoon; follow-up in 2 days.
Pneumococcal vaccine once recovered.

medications.name: acetaminophen
medications.frequency: up to every 8 hours as needed for fever

follow_up.text: Follow-up visit in 2 days; x-ray result by phone this afternoon.

saved_note.patient_instructions: You likely have pneumonia in your right lung. Get a chest x-ray and blood tests today. Take amoxicillin-clavulanate 875 mg twice a day and clarithromycin 500 mg twice a day, both for 7 days. Keep taking all your heart medicines as before, including simvastatin at night. Drink fluids, but stay within your usual limit of about 2 liters a day. You can take acetaminophen for fever, up to 1,000 mg every 8 hours. Check your oxygen with the finger monitor twice a day. Go to the emergency room if your breathing gets worse, your oxygen drops below 92, you feel confused, or you can't keep fluids down. We will call you with your x-ray result this afternoon. Come back in 2 days. Once you feel better, we will give you the pneumonia vaccine.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Mr. Whitfield, come on in. What's going on?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I've had this cough for five days, and the last two days I've had fevers and chills.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Are you bringing anything up when you cough?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yeah, thick yellow-green stuff. And it hurts on the right side when I take a deep breath.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Any shortness of breath?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: More than usual. I get winded walking to the mailbox.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: With your heart failure, I want to make sure this isn't fluid. Any leg swelling or weight gain?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: My weight's been steady at 204 pounds. My ankles look the same as always.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Are you sleeping flat, or do you need more pillows?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Same two pillows as always.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Have you been around anyone who's sick?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: My grandson had a bad cold last week.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And you're still not smoking?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Not since I quit, eleven years ago now.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good. Let me listen. Your temperature is 100.9, heart rate 92, breathing 20 a minute, blood pressure 128/78, and your oxygen is 94%. I hear crackles at the right lung base. Heart sounds are regular, with no new murmur. There's trace ankle swelling, the same as last time.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I think you have pneumonia in the right lower lung. I'd like a chest x-ray today to confirm, and a blood count and a basic metabolic panel.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Do I need to go to the hospital?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Your oxygen and blood pressure are okay, so we can treat you at home, but I want to watch you closely.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I'm going to start Augmentin, 875 mg twice a day, plus clarithromycin, 500 mg twice a day, both for 7 days.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Okay. Should I keep taking all my heart pills?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes. Keep the carvedilol 12.5 twice a day, the furosemide 40 in the morning, the lisinopril 20, the spironolactone 25, and the potassium, 20 milliequivalents a day.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And the simvastatin at night?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes, the simvastatin 40 at night too.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: All right.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Drink fluids, but stay within your usual limit of about 2 liters a day because of your heart. Use acetaminophen for fever, up to 1,000 mg every 8 hours.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: If your breathing gets worse, your oxygen at home drops below 92, or you get confused or can't keep fluids down, go to the emergency room.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: My wife has one of those finger oxygen things.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Perfect. Check it twice a day. We'll call you with the x-ray result this afternoon, and I want to see you back in 2 days.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And once you're feeling better, we should get you the pneumonia vaccine.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Okay, thank you.
